sections.heading: What is Checkout Abandonment Rate?
paragraphs: Checkout Abandonment Rate measures the percentage of shoppers who start the checkout process but leave before completing their purchase. Unlike cart abandonment (which tracks all created carts), checkout abandonment specifically focuses on users who demonstrated clear purchase intent by initiating checkout. The global average checkout abandonment rate is approximately 75.19%.

sections.heading: Checkout vs Cart Abandonment
paragraphs: Measures shoppers who add items to cart but never proceed to checkout. Includes window shoppers and price comparers.
Measures shoppers who start checkout but don't complete it. These users showed clear purchase intent, making this more actionable for optimization.

sections.heading: How to Calculate Checkout Abandonment Rate
paragraphs: Example: If 100 customers begin checkout but only 30 complete their purchase:
sections.formula: Rate = ((Checkouts Started - Checkouts Completed) / Checkouts Started) × 100

bullets.label: Streamline Checkout
bullets.text: 1. Keep to 12-14 form elements max, or 7-8 actual fields. Each extra step increases abandonment.

bullets.label: Show Costs Early
bullets.text: 2. Display shipping, taxes, and fees before checkout. Surprises cause 48% of abandonments.

bullets.label: Offer Guest Checkout
bullets.text: 3. Requiring account creation increases abandonment by 35%.

bullets.label: Add Progress Indicators
bullets.text: 4. Show users where they are in the checkout process.

bullets.label: Optimize for Mobile
bullets.text: 5. Mobile abandonment is 17% higher. Prioritize mobile-first design.

bullets.label: Display Trust Signals
bullets.text: 6. Security badges and payment icons reduce trust concerns.
